summary: Ngawang Lek Shé Gyatso studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Trulshik Rinpoche.
Ngawang Norbu studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.
A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Ngawang Nyima studied under the 13th and 14th Dalai Lamas and Trijang Rinpoche. He served as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Monastery.

Ngawang Samten works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery and CIHTS, where he was Director (attested 1990–2019), and held visiting posts at Smith, Hampshire, Amherst, and the University of Tasmania.
Ngorpa Pönlob Lo Ter Wangpo studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and later taught Shenphen Nangwa and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Ngulchu Dharmabhadra studied at Tashi Gephel Monastery around 1787 and under teachers including Yeshe Paldrup, Lobzang Tsultrim, Ngulchu Ngawang Dorje, and Lobpön Lozang Gyaltsen.
A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Nguyen Thi Tuyet earned a PhD from Punjabi University (attested 2012) under Inder Mohan Singh, and also studied under Thich Nu Bao Nguyet.
Nguyen Van Hoa works in Buddhist studies and Indology, completing a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University under the supervision of Shailaja Bapat and Lata Chhatre.
A scholar of Buddhist studies, Nguyen Van Thuong studied at the University of Delhi under MA supervisor K. T. S. Sarao.

Nianzu Huang worked in Buddhist studies, studying at Beijing Institute of Technology and under Lianju Xia, Gongga Rinpoche, and Hsu Yun. He headed the Central Broadcasting System and became a professor at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications around 1955.
Working in religious and Buddhist studies, Nichidatsu Fujii studied at Rissho University, Taisho University, Kogi Shingonshu Rengo Daigaku, Horyu-ji, and Kennin-ji, and founded Nipponzan-Myōhōji.

Nicholas Dirks works in Indology and history/archaeology. After studying at Wesleyan and the University of Chicago, he held posts at Caltech (~1986–1987), the University of Michigan (~1987–1997), and Columbia University (~1997–2013).

A scholar of Indology and history/archaeology, Allen studied at Oxford and SOAS under Rodney Needham. He taught at Durham University (1972–1976) and Oxford, serving as Lecturer and later Reader in the Social Anthropology of South Asia.

Nicholas Poppe specialized in linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies, studying at Saint Petersburg State University under Boris Vladimirtsov. He held professorships at Saint Petersburg State University (1923, 1925–1941) and served on the faculty at the University of Washington (1949–1968).

Working in history/archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and religious studies, Roerich studied at Saint Petersburg State University and the Imperial Academy of Arts. He directed the Imperial Society for the Encouragement of the Arts and founded Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute.
Nicholas Witkowski works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at Stanford University by 2015 and was a research fellow at the University of Tokyo (attested 2017).
Nicholson T. Collier works in religious and Buddhist studies and completed a PhD at the University of Chicago under the supervision of Paul J. Griffiths.
A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Nicola Bajetta is affiliated with the University of Hamburg as a doctoral local researcher and project staff member (attested 2026).

Working in Iranian/Central Asian studies, Sinology, and history, Di Cosmo earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington. He held positions at Cambridge, Harvard, and Columbia, and became Henry Luce Foundation Professor at the Institute for Advanced Study around 2003.

Nicolaas Johannes Krom worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served at the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies (1913–1916) and held posts at Leiden University in 1919 and from 1925 to 1945.
